items.title: Airbnb says it's launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
items.snippet: Airbnb says its upcoming AI agent will help travelers plan trips, compare options, manage bookings, and get assistance throughout their stay.

items.title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots
items.snippet: Serve Robotics announced alonsgside its third-quarter earnings that it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services to offer customers its connectivity and data tools.

items.title: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar
items.snippet: Meta's AI agent can now take calls as a customizable animated avatar, ahead of the launch of a Tamagotchi-like wearable designed to bring Muse to life.

items.title: Meta warns that election backlash against data centers could make AI expansion harder
items.snippet: Meta warns that growing political opposition to data centers could threaten future AI investments, as communities push back against massive infrastructure projects.

items.title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
items.snippet: OpenAI's newest cybersecurity model comes out as AI labs face scrutiny of their work to protect digital infrastructure.

items.title: US government warns of 'ongoing cyber threat' amid mass hacks of industrial retail and military freezers
items.snippet: A joint U.S. government statement says the hacks are affecting the food, transportation, and healthcare industries after reports of global mass hacks.

items.title: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027
items.snippet: Speaking at a Wall Street Journal tech conference on Wednesday, the executive touted how the company had been gaining ground in the enterprise market, where rival Anthropic had already successfully made inroads.

items.title: The ex-Secret Service agent who flipped a hacker is now raising a second $250M cybersecurity fund
items.snippet: Stephen Ward, a former Secret Service agent and Home Depot CISO, is preparing a second fund of roughly $250 million for Brightmind Partners.

items.title: Claude can now analyze your spending with its new Personal Finance tool
items.snippet: With Personal Finance in Claude, users can connect their bank and card accounts through Plaid and ask questions about their finances.

items.title: Harbinger raises $240M after expanding into defense
items.snippet: The Los Angeles-based startup has now raised more than $650 million, and is working on electric trucks, emergency vehicles, and a driverless platform for the military.

items.title: Google's Ocarina of Time easter egg is a blast from the past
items.snippet: If you’re sick of AI search and all the business of modern Google search, this week’s Google easter egg will take you back 28 years to a simpler time when Ocarina of Time was the pinnacle of gaming, and Google was still a new name. It’s hard to believe I was sitting on a couch in my parents’ living room 28 years ago, playing Ocarina of Time on my Nintendo 64. Apparently, the folks at Google feel just as nostalgic as I do about the upcoming release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo Switch 2. Case in point, if you go to Google right now and search for “Zelda” or “Ocarina of Time,” you’ll see a Master Sword appear in the bottom-right corner of your screen. Tap that sword, and you’ll be magically transported back to the way Google looked back in 1998. It’s just seven blue links with short descriptions on a very simple page. Even the “I’m Feeling Lucky” button works! Unfortunately, the theme only works for this specific search, so you can’t keep things looking retro if you search for anything else, even if you start from the old-school search box on the 1998-themed…

items.snippet: AT&T's smart home security system now integrates with Gemini for Home. items.title: Prevent Siri and Search From Accessing Specific iPhone Apps
items.snippet: In iOS 27.2, Apple has a new settings menu that lets you choose which apps Siri, Search, and suggestions can access, all from one list. Here's what's changed and how to use the new menu. With iOS 27.2, Apple has replaced the old App Access controls with a redesigned Excluded Apps feature that makes it a lot simpler to keep specific apps away from Siri, Search, and suggestions. It's actually a bigger change than it might sound. Previously, excluding an app in iOS meant opening Settings ➝ Apple Intelligence & Siri ➝ Apps and adjusting each app's toggles individually. The country is also looking to commercialize its SHAKTI and VEGA RISC-V processors, expand domestic server production, and attract more semiconductor investment. items.title: Zoom Window disappears when monitors change
